title: Three-Way Word Embeddings for Polingual: Script, Sound and Meaning, and a Re-Ranked Lexicon
description: Polingual translates single words offline from a Wiktionary lexicon for 28 languages. The lexicon lists English meanings in English frequency order, so a rare sense can come first: Hebrew akhil (edible) was the first translation of English good. We embed 529,131 words of 29 languages four ways: rendered script pixels with a small CNN, character n-grams, phonetic features from Wiktionary IPA with a grapheme model for words without IPA, and LaBSE meaning vectors, plus a joint projection of all four. Meaning vectors then re-rank every translation pair, with gloss senses added as candidates. On the held-out half of an independent Tatoeba-aligned word set, the first English sense shown is right for 68.3% of words, up from 58.0%. For English to target words, a model audit of 100 changed first answers finds 91 right after re-ranking and 60 before. Language graphs drawn from the embeddings show script similarity staying inside a script family while phonetic similarity crosses scripts. Every definition has a Lean 4 counterpart.
